OPERATION GREEN LANTERN
Syria / fictional Latakia-area rescue / single-player flight of three OH-58Ds

You are Anvil 1-1, with engines running on the four-pad FARP HAVEN, approximately 13 nautical miles southwest of the pickup-zone center. You lead Anvil 1 with two AI OH-58D wingmen: Anvil 1-2 carries guns and Hellfires; Anvil 1-3 carries guns and rockets. All three aircraft start hot on separate numbered landing pads at FARP HAVEN. Check systems and weapons, then depart when ready. Use the normal wingman radio commands to direct attacks or rejoin. FARP ATC: HAVEN 128.500 MHz AM; LANTERN 127.500 MHz AM. Both FARPs provide fuel, ammunition, repairs and ground power. Park on or close to the pad and use the Ground Crew radio menu; shut down for repairs. Fly the route toward WP2, then WP3. Plan about 9 minutes inbound at 90 knots, plus preflight checks, extraction and approximately 17 minutes outbound to FARP LANTERN. Guardian launches from STENNIS when you lift off, and BRUISER launches three minutes later; the pursuit waits for your approach. You can launch Guardian earlier using F10 Other > GREEN LANTERN > Air Support > Launch carrier package.

MISSION
Recover downed pilot Sparrow, then land in the BLUE-smoke recovery area at WP4 (FARP LANTERN casualty collection point, approximately 25 nm southwest of the pickup area). LANTERN is a separate field site with a landing pad, medical tent and support vehicle. After pickup, fly southwest into friendly territory for medical handover. WP3 is only an approximate last-known position. Sparrow is randomized onto a safe landing site within 200 m of WP3 each mission start. His exact unit icon and position are hidden on the F10 map; the search marker stays at WP3. When within 2 km of the search area, use F10 Other > GREEN LANTERN > Rescue > Request survivor smoke (green), then visually locate him. There is no green smoke until requested.

PICKUP
Land within 400 m of Sparrow, below 1 m/s ground speed, and remain still. Pickup is automatic and simulated: hold for 20 seconds within 100 m, with additional approach time at 3 m/s beyond that distance (up to two minutes total at 400 m). The run and boarding are simulated; no passenger animation or native troop-carrying feature is required. Moving or taking off resets the timer. At FARP LANTERN, follow blue smoke to the marked pad and hold on the ground for 15 seconds within 100 m to complete the rescue.

COORDINATION
Two F/A-18Cs, Guardian, are based aboard USS STENNIS, initially 90 nm northwest of the extraction area. Request the air package before departure using F10; the shorter inbound route from HAVEN takes less time than the carrier aircraft transit. Automatic launch at your takeoff remains a fallback. Allow approximately 15-20 minutes for launch, climb and transit. Depart HAVEN at about 90 knots and hold at the IP if Guardian has not checked in. An E-2C Hawkeye, OVERLORD, launches from STENNIS at mission start and establishes an offshore radar orbit at about 25,000 ft. Contact AWACS on 251.000 MHz AM via the normal radio menu.

Wave 1: WEASEL (two F/A-18Cs, two AGM-88C HARMs each) launches with Guardian and attacks the radar-guided coastal SA-6. F10 offers a generic WEASEL radar-suppression request. A confirmed tracking-radar kill is reported; radar silence alone is not confirmation. HARMs cannot defeat the IR-guided Strela-10, which remains a BRUISER or Kiowa target.

Guardian conducts the fighter sweep and provides air cover against MiGs, holds on station for up to 20 minutes unless fuel or combat requires earlier recovery, and returns to STENNIS. Wave 2: BRUISER, two F/A-18Cs with four AGM-65F Mavericks each and internal guns, launches three minutes after Guardian. They hold southwest of extraction awaiting your clearance. F10 Other > GREEN LANTERN > Air Support offers Request CAS near me, Request radar suppression, and Hold fire / cancel CAS. A request assigns a 5 km search area centered on your position at the time of the call; it does not reveal enemy unit names, group names or target counts. Move to a useful observation position before requesting support. Requests are queued until BRUISER is within 20 km of targets in that area. Attack assignments are deferred if an enemy vehicle is within 700 m of Sparrow or either OH-58. This is a scripted separation check, not a guarantee against collateral damage after weapons release. Both flights recover aboard STENNIS. The carrier maintains a steady flight-operations course; its distance changes during the sortie. STENNIS: TACAN 74X, ICLS 11, ATC 127.500 MHz AM.

THREATS
Two pairs of DShK technicals begin hunting Sparrow when you enter 8 km. A western patrol adds two more technicals; an eastern checkpoint has two BRDM-2 scout cars and two trucks. Four minutes after the hunt starts, two technicals and two trucks reinforce the area. Destroying every vehicle is optional; prioritize clearing the pickup and recovering Sparrow. Two Mi-24V Hinds activate at the same gate and patrol east/south of extraction, searching for your helicopters. They carry rockets and cannon; Guardian can engage them when detected. Two MiG-29s launch into the fight 75 seconds after you cross 6 km from the pickup-zone center, attempting to penetrate the extraction area. Coastal air defenses: an SA-6 battery north of Latakia (one tracking radar and three launchers) and a Strela-10 team west of extraction, each with a soft support truck. Their positions are taken from existing Syria mission ground placements. Bruiser transits at 2500 m MSL and can face short-range SAM fire; Guardian remains higher for the fighter sweep. Use WEASEL radar suppression for radar threats. BRUISER requests cover the area near your helicopter, allowing you to request support against threats you encounter along the route. Killing the support truck does not neutralize the missile launcher. The technicals can kill Sparrow; a vehicle within 80 m for 20 seconds also captures him. Prioritize the rescue over destroying every enemy.

LOADOUT / COMMS
OH-58D: Anvil 1-1 and 1-2 each carry two AGM-114K Hellfires and an M3P .50-cal gun with 500 rounds. Anvil 1-3 carries the same gun plus seven M151 rockets. All three carry 30 flares and 270 kg fuel (about 81% of the 333.69 kg tank capacity). This is a fuel-capacity check, not a verified gross-weight or hover-performance check. Check the DCS loadout weight and cockpit performance calculations before takeoff. Plan approximately 25 minutes cruise plus ground time, combat and recovery. Monitor actual fuel time remaining and preserve a 20-minute reserve; shorten the attack or divert to LANTERN if needed. Use the MMS laser to designate light vehicles. Guardian: air-to-air loadout with two external fuel tanks for the carrier transit. UHF 251.000 MHz AM. Scripted coordination appears as text; no voice files. F10 Other > GREEN LANTERN > Rescue provides Status / return directions, Request survivor smoke (green), and Request recovery smoke (blue). Blue smoke is renewed when Sparrow boards and every four minutes during the return leg; WP4 marks the recovery area, while the F10 LANTERN marker identifies the actual terrain-checked pad.

CONDITIONS
Unit labels are forced OFF. The F10 map is restricted to friendly units only; enemy assets are hidden. The approximate Sparrow search-area marker and the LANTERN marker remain available. 08:00 local, clear, light wind, QNH 1013 hPa / 29.92 inHg. Rescue fails if Sparrow is killed/captured, your helicopter is destroyed, or 25 minutes elapse after the hunt starts without pickup. A successful return sets mission-success flag 902; failure sets 903. Flying continues after the result.

Requires Syria and OH-58D. No UH-60L, MIST, MOOSE, or other mod required. Terrain positions and AI behavior still require an in-simulator flight check.
